issue.body:
**Owner direction, 2026-10-05:** write the software side of the Mark II split now, in parallel with the protocol-processor program. The requirement change (#664) still waits for the PP program to finish.

## Scope

Bare-metal firmware on the on-chip RISC-V for:
- **ADP**;
- **ACMP** (decided earlier the same day);
- **MAAP**;
- **SRP** (MRP, with MSRP and MVRP);
- **AECP**: descriptor serving, commands, and the unsolicited notifications. The owner added AECP the same day;
- **the NV memory handling**: read the saved entity state from the flash at boot, apply it, and write it back on change (the #70 saved-state design).

It sits behind the packet-mailbox and ingress-filter contract recorded on #640: block RAM rings, doorbell and interrupt, 32-bit accesses, no DMA, a bus adapter per host, portable C behind a small HAL, one YAML contract. It must port to a hard core.

The fabric keeps:
- framing and timestamps;
- the gPTP plane;
- the timers that carry hard deadlines, posted to the core as events;
- the ingress filter.

## Rules while #664 is open

- Everything lands behind a build switch whose default is the current all-fabric placement. No shipping-image change.
- The firmware builds and is tested on the host against a mailbox model. The existing processor suites' stimulus is reused through that model wherever possible, so each protocol's checks carry over.
- Each protocol states its firmware service-latency bound per response path and tests it, as NFR-SCOUT-03 will require after #664.
- Portable C (C11), no compiler intrinsics in protocol code, and a fixed-width, byte-order-explicit wire layer.

## Lanes (in order)

- **F0, the contract and harness (first).** The mailbox and ingress-filter YAML contract and its generator (fabric module skeleton, C header, docs), the HAL, the host mailbox model and test harness. The ADP firmware is the first vertical slice through it.
- **F1, NV memory handling.** Flash read at boot, validation per the #70 saved-state format (KLJ2), apply, and the write and commit path, ported from `sw/firmware/milan_baremetal` and the processor writer's rules. It can start alongside F0 against the HAL draft.
- **F2, MAAP.**
- **F3, ACMP.**
- **F4, SRP (MRP, MSRP, MVRP).**
- **F5, AECP** (descriptor serving, commands, notifications).

F2 to F5 start once F0's contract merges, so the protocols share one interface.

Relates to #640, #664, #70, and milestone 13.

decisions.body:
[A10] **Round 3 for [A582] on PR #704** (F-INT PR 1), head `25bbe4d9`. [R582-1](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/pull/704#issuecomment-6092077028) (one MAJOR, two MINOR) and [R583-1](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/pull/704#issuecomment-6091895255) (three MINOR) are NEGATIVE. Both judge the block, its generator, the writers' ordering and the SRP test hold sound. The gaps are values the block does not yet carry. My ruling 6088423771 copied an incomplete list; these findings complete it.

1. **R582-1-F1 (MAJOR): publish each sink's started level.**
   - It is the level the datapath combines with BOUND for listener accept (`milan_datapath.sv:5375`, `:6270`, `:5886`; Milan v1.2 5.3.8.7).
   - The ACMP owner writes it before the BIND_RX response that echoes it, and before any later move is reported.
   - Give it the same RTL checks, model twin, writer ordering test and three plants (moved, wrong field, skipped) as the other values.
2. **R582-1-F2 = R583-1-F1: publish each source's Talker-declared level.**
   - The datapath's CRF tagging interlock reads it (`:5677-5678`, `:6225`; IEEE 802.1Q-2018 35.1.2).
   - The SRP owner writes it before the declaration it describes is sent. Same checks, and the same three plants.
3. **Completeness by construction.** Add R583-1's `consumer_census.py`, or an equivalent, as a standing check. Every wire-affecting read of a processor class-D output in `milan_datapath.sv` must map to a block field or a named, ruled exclusion, and the check fails on an unmapped read. A planted unmapped read must be caught. Then correct the completeness text in MAILBOX_SPLIT.md, ARCHITECTURE_HW_SW_SPLIT.md and the PR body.
4. **R582-1-F3: `DA_GATE` keeps its current meaning (DA validity), recorded as a public choice.**
   - The processor's `acmp_declaring_o` also requires a probe within T-SRP-DAFRESH or a registered Listener (Milan v1.2 4.3.3.1, per processor `05_acmp_engine.md:405`). The firmware ACMP core does not implement that predicate yet. Adding it is new protocol behaviour and does not belong in this PR.
   - The contract text must stop claiming equivalence with `acmp_declaring_o`, and the design page's choices list must name the egress consequence.
   - A separate lane, F3b, adds the predicate to the firmware ACMP talker and changes `DA_GATE` to publish it. F3b lands before PR 2, so PR 2's comparison never meets this difference.
5. **R583-1-F2:** add a named two-interface test in which interface 1 acquires, and each interface's `DA_GATE` is asserted on its own, before its own report. `rv-maap-gate-on-interface-0` joins `ctrl_mutants.py` and must be killed by that test.
6. **R583-1-F3:** both harness views and every user use `idle_slope_bps`.

Keep the memory discipline from your last session (16 GB cap, one Verilator build at a time). Commit on `25bbe4d9` with no rebase or amend. The all-fabric default stays byte-identical. Post REVIEW READY with the head.

[A10] **F3b, the milan-fpga half.** This lane follows ruling [6092086337](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/665#issuecomment-6092086337), item 4. The core half merged in tsn-c-stack #25 as `70936b77`: the firmware ACMP talker now declares only after a probe within T-SRP-DAFRESH (15 s) or with a registered Listener (Milan v1.2 4.3.3.1). This half moves the pin and makes `DA_GATE` publish that predicate, before F-INT PR 2. Executor [A612].

**Base.** PR #705's reviewed head `d40e4e98` (697c, which adds the tsn-c-stack submodule; its act is running), on branch `665-f3b-parent`. Once #705 merges, the manager merges dev into this branch.

1. **Pin.**
   - Move `third_party/tsn-c-stack` from the 697c pin to `70936b77`.
   - Prove the stack difference between the two pins is exactly tsn-c-stack #25: list the commits and files.
   - The cores the parent builds change only by the F3b predicate.
2. **`DA_GATE` publishes the predicate.**
   - `DA_GATE` asserts only when DA is valid *and* (a probe arrived within T-SRP-DAFRESH *or* a Listener is registered). That matches the processor's `acmp_declaring_o` (processor `05_acmp_engine.md:405`).
   - The contract text now states that equivalence, and the design page's choices list drops the egress consequence that ruling item 4 recorded.
3. **Tests and controls.**
   - One firmware control per arm: a fresh probe, a registered Listener, neither (not declaring), and a probe aged past 15 s (stops declaring).
   - Keep the two-interface `DA_GATE` test (ruling item 5).
   - Planted mutants on each arm are killed.
   - Where a differential against `acmp_declaring_o` exists, it now agrees on all arms.
4. **Images.**
   - Record the image hash table for every shape, before and after.
   - The all-fabric default shape stays byte-identical; STOP if it cannot.
   - The Release image growth is within the ceiling of ruling [6126295947](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/665#issuecomment-6126295947) (the ceiling applies to Release only).
5. **Gates.** Every gate the change touches passes, never piped, and the coverage tables are recorded.

Post REVIEW READY (or STOP) with the head. Do not push.

[A10] **F3b ruling on [A612] STOP [6151402754](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/665#issuecomment-6151402754).** All three blockers are the manager's assignment errors. Corrected assignment:

1. **Pin scope, revised.** I scoped the pin wrongly. The move goes to `70936b77`, and it brings every reviewed, merged tsn-c-stack change between the 697c pin `405dc683` and that target: #25 (the F3b predicate), plus #19 (malformed ADP discovery) and #20 (entity generation).
   - In HANDOFF.md, list each stack PR in that range with its merge commit and its review links.
   - Record each parent-visible effect, including the ADP minimum frame length, version and control-data-length refusals, with a parent-harness test (`sw/firmware/ctrl/test/…`) showing the behaviour at the new pin.
   - No other stack change is allowed. If the range holds anything unmerged or unreviewed, STOP.
2. **Behaviour-change exception.** In this lane, firmware behaviour may change in exactly two ways: the `DA_GATE` predicate (`maap_mbx.c:62` and its contract) and the pinned stack's listed changes. Any other firmware behaviour change is a STOP.
   - The all-fabric default shape stays byte-identical.
   - The firmware images change, and their hash table before and after goes in HANDOFF.md.
3. **Release ceiling.** The ruling is [tsn-c-stack #24, comment 6126295947](https://github.com/kebag-logic/tsn-c-stack/issues/24#issuecomment-6126295947): the ceiling applies to the Release image only. Record the growth against it.

Everything else in the assignment ([6151273346](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/665#issuecomment-6151273346)) stands. Executor [A612]. Post REVIEW READY (or STOP) with the head.

release-ceiling.body: [A10] **Ruling on the [A606 STOP](https://github.com/kebag-logic/tsn-c-stack/issues/24#issuecomment-6126278688).** The 2 KB ceiling in the assignment applies to the shipping (Release) bare-metal image only, measured at 1,296 bytes, which is within it. The Debug figure (+2,168 bytes) is reported in the handoff and is not a limit. Continue from the uncommitted candidate: commit it, run the full validation campaign, the mutation plants and the test-removal escapes, and post REVIEW READY (or STOP) with the head.

stack-integration-record.body:
[A10] Merge bar met for the integration of #21:
- PR #22 at `405dc683` (the commit milan-fpga #697 pins): [R622-4](https://github.com/kebag-logic/tsn-c-stack/pull/22#issuecomment-6116467700) and [R623-5](https://github.com/kebag-logic/tsn-c-stack/pull/22#issuecomment-6116469528) are both POSITIVE at this head.
- This PR, #23, merges that head into main `98dc9e3` at `3c9ca52f`. Both reviews state a separate POSITIVE verdict on it: every conflict with #19 and #20 is resolved, generated documents are regenerated, and all gates pass on both targets.
- Hosted quality and bare-metal are green on both PRs.

Merging #23 with a merge commit puts #22's head into main's history, which completes #21.
